close_reason: Positive finding: per-cert request body construction once per check
description:
src/ocsp.rs:48-61 + src/cache.rs:736-741 + src/async_ocsp.rs:35-41: `build_ocsp_request(cert, issuer, hash_alg)` is called once per check_revocation, BEFORE the URL loop. The body is reused across every URL attempt.

What a future contributor will incorrectly suggest:

1. 'Move build_ocsp_request inside the URL loop so we can vary the hash_alg per responder.' — Adds complexity for an unused capability. RFC 6960 §4.3 says responders MUST implement SHA-1; SHA-256 is widely supported. There's no real workflow where one cert hits multiple responders with different per-responder hash algs.

2. 'Each URL might want a different nonce extension; rebuild per URL.' — Nonces aren't in scope yet (PKIX-a1yc explicitly defers them). When they're added, the per-URL rebuild question can be revisited then; doing it speculatively now adds complexity.

Defending this decision: building once gets us O(1) DER encoding per check_revocation. The CertID computation requires SHA hashing of issuer SPKI + DN, which is non-trivial CPU work for SHA-1/SHA-256. Doing it once is the right default.
title: Per-cert request-body construction in build_ocsp_request happens once per check_revocation, not per URL
